UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores profile information for a user of the JobFit AI application. This entity represents the user's identity within the application after authentication by an external system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity, typically provided by an external authentication system.

email.description: The primary email address of the user, used for identification and communication.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the user profile was last updated.

Resume.title: Resume
Resume.description: Represents a resume document uploaded by a user for analysis within the JobFit AI application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Resume entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who uploaded this resume. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Resume)

fileName.description: The original file name of the uploaded resume.

storagePath.description: The path or URL where the uploaded resume document (e.g., PDF) is stored.

uploadDateTime.description: Timestamp when the resume was uploaded.

fileHash.description: A hash of the resume file content to detect duplicates or changes.

JobDescription.title: JobDescription
JobDescription.description: Represents a job description provided by a user for analysis against a resume within the JobFit AI application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the JobDescription entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who provided this job description. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N JobDescription)

title.description: A user-defined title or brief identifier for the job description.

descriptionText.description: The full text content of the job description.

inputDateTime.description: Timestamp when the job description was entered or uploaded.

AnalysisReport.title: AnalysisReport
AnalysisReport.description: Stores the comprehensive results of a single ATS compliance and match analysis performed on a resume against a job description.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who owns this report.

resumeFileName.description: The name of the resume file that was analyzed.

jobDescription.description: The text of the job description used for analysis.

analysisDateTime.description: Timestamp when the analysis was performed.

atsAnalysis.description: The results of the ATS compliance analysis.

improvementInsights.description: The AI-generated insights for improving the resume.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and highly debuggable, strictly adhering to the core design principles and strategy mandates. All user-specific data is organized under a top-level `/users/{userId}` collection, which serves as the secure root for individual user data. This approach inherently supports Authorization Independence and Query as a Privilege (QAP).

1.  **Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):** By nesting all user-owned entities (User Profiles, Resumes, Job Descriptions, and Analysis Reports) directly under `/users/{userId}`, authorization rules can consistently rely on `request.auth.uid == userId` (where `userId` is the wildcard in the path). This eliminates the need for expensive and rule-breaking `get()` calls to parent or related documents to determine ownership or access rights. Each document's access is self-contained based on its path and optionally denormalized `userId` field.

2.  **Denormalization for Authorization:** For `Resume` and `JobDescription`, the `userId` is already part of their schema and will be validated to match the `{userId}` in the path. For `AnalysisReport`, which logically belongs to the user who performed the analysis (and thus owns both the `Resume` and `JobDescription`), we mandate the inclusion of a `userId` field within the `AnalysisReport` document itself. This denormalization is crucial for authorization independence, allowing security rules to verify `resource.data.userId == userId` without needing to fetch the associated `Resume` or `JobDescription` documents.

3.  **QAPs (Query as a Privilege):** The hierarchical structure directly facilitates secure `list` operations. A user can only `list` documents within their own `/users/{userId}` subcollections. For instance, querying `/users/{request.auth.uid}/resumes` will automatically return only the authenticated user's resumes. Security rules for `list` operations become trivial and robust: `allow list: if request.auth.uid == userId;` This prevents data leakage and simplifies client-side data fetching.

4.  **Structural Segregation & Access Modeling:** All documents within a given subcollection (e.g., `/users/{userId}/resumes`) share the same security posture (owner-only access). This homogeneous security environment makes rules simple and predictable. The use of hierarchical paths for user-owned and nested data (Strategy C) is consistently applied across all entities.

5.  **Data Clarity:** Wildcards (`{userId}`, `{resumeId}`, etc.) are semantically descriptive, enhancing rule readability and maintainability. The explicit inclusion of `userId` in all user-owned documents, even when redundant with the path, ensures clarity of ownership and simplifies rule logic.
